Done. The merged, sharded checkpoint is in `out/T5/`, produced by a single execution of `out/T5/solution.py`.

**What the solution does.** It reads the base and adapter with safetensors, groups the 24 adapter tensors into 12 A/B pairs by regex, computes `2 * (B @ A)` in float32, transposes it because `fan_in_fan_out` is true, adds it to the Conv1D weight, and packs tensors greedily into shards under the 100 MiB budget. The four required checks abort the run before writing if they fail.

**Result.**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Executions | 1, no failures |
| Shards | 5, with `wte.weight` alone in the last |
| Unchanged tensors bit-exact | 148 of 148 |
| Merged weights vs float64 recomputation | relative error 2.6e-8 |
| Merged weights vs peft `merge_and_unload` | relative error 0.0 |

**Why a plain script rather than peft.** The base keys have no `transformer.` prefix and include the `attn.bias` mask buffers, so saving through transformers would rename keys and drop 12 tensors. Peft also cannot match these adapter keys to the HF module paths and silently loads a zero adapter. I used peft only as an in-memory cross-check after the run.

The self-report with tools used, pitfalls, and the config discrepancy on `target_modules` is in `out/T5/REPORT.md`.
